label: Home
headline: Help your home notice trouble sooner.
description: Explore practical technology for water, fire, security, air quality, and properties that are sometimes empty.

concerns.label: Water
concerns.why: A whole-home system can watch water flow, alert you to unusual activity, and—when supported—close the main valve.
stages: An alert or automatic shutoff responds

concerns.label: Fire + electrical
concerns.prompt: Get earlier warning of smoke, CO, or electrical hazards
concerns.why: Connected alarms and electrical-monitoring services can add remote awareness, but they do not replace required life-safety devices or professional repair.
stages: People are alerted and can respond

concerns.label: Security
concerns.why: Connected security can combine entry sensors, cameras, and optional professional monitoring while keeping subscription and privacy tradeoffs visible.
stages: A sensor or camera reports it
You or a monitoring service reviews the alert

concerns.label: Away from home
concerns.prompt: Keep watch while a property is empty
concerns.why: Water, temperature, entry, and power alerts can help surface problems while nobody is there.
stages: A condition moves outside your limits
A remote alert creates a chance to investigate

concerns.label: Garage + access
concerns.prompt: Know whether an access point was left open
concerns.why: Connected garage and access devices can report state and support remote control, but mechanical compatibility and account security require verification.
stages: You review the alert before acting

concerns.label: Temperature
concerns.prompt: Notice heating or cooling trouble while away
concerns.why: Temperature sensors can flag conditions that may threaten plumbing, comfort, pets, or stored property without diagnosing the equipment failure.
stages: Temperature moves outside a set range
An alert creates a chance to investigate

label: Vehicle
headline: Give your vehicle better memory and awareness.
description: Compare incident recording, theft tracking, driver alerts, diagnostics, and maintenance tools without turning this into an insurance quote.

concerns.label: Incident recording
concerns.prompt: Document what happens on the road
concerns.why: Dash cameras differ meaningfully in video quality, field of view, parking behavior, power, storage, and subscription features.
stages: The camera detects or records it
The saved video can be reviewed

concerns.label: Theft tracking
concerns.prompt: Receive movement alerts and locate a vehicle
concerns.why: Dedicated cellular GPS tools can report location and suspicious movement, but coverage, power, tampering, and subscriptions matter.
stages: Location information may support a response

concerns.label: Teen driver
concerns.prompt: Share driving alerts with clear household consent
concerns.why: Some connected-vehicle tools can report trips, speed, braking, or geofences. Everyone being monitored should understand the setup.

concerns.label: Diagnostics
concerns.prompt: Translate warning lights and maintenance signals
concerns.why: OBD tools can make vehicle codes easier to understand, but they do not replace manufacturer warnings or a qualified repair diagnosis.
stages: You decide whether professional service is needed

concerns.label: Tires
concerns.prompt: Keep tire condition and pressure visible
concerns.why: Vehicle and aftermarket systems may surface pressure or condition information, but compatibility and recommended manual inspection still matter.

concerns.label: Emergency help
concerns.why: Some vehicle and phone services can help request assistance after an incident, subject to coverage, subscription, device power, and service limitations.
stages: A supported system detects or receives a request
Location and event context may reach a response service

concerns.label: EV charging
concerns.prompt: Monitor charging without overlooking electrical fit
concerns.why: Connected chargers can schedule and report sessions, but circuit capacity, installation, vehicle compatibility, and utility programs need independent verification.
stages: The charger manages and records the session
Alerts or schedules help the owner respond

label: Family
headline: Make invisible conditions easier to notice.
description: A carefully bounded starting point for household air, environmental awareness, and consent-based alerts—not medical advice or guaranteed emergency response.

concerns.label: Air quality
concerns.prompt: See indoor air and radon conditions over time
concerns.why: Multi-sensor monitors can make radon, particulate matter, carbon dioxide, VOC, humidity, and temperature trends visible.
stages: The app provides readings and alerts

concerns.label: Household alerts
concerns.prompt: Keep important home alerts in one place
concerns.why: Connected smoke, CO, water, and security alerts can improve remote awareness, subject to connectivity and device limitations.
stages: A household member receives an alert

label: Business
headline: Monitor the conditions your operation depends on.
description: Starter guidance for water, temperature, and facility awareness. These tools do not replace code, inspections, or commercial risk engineering.

concerns.label: Temperature
concerns.prompt: Watch refrigeration or environmental conditions remotely
concerns.why: Commercial sensors can record temperature and send alerts when readings move outside configured limits.
stages: An alert creates a chance to investigate

concerns.label: Water
concerns.prompt: Detect water near equipment or inventory
concerns.why: Commercial leak sensors can report water at selected locations, but detection-only devices do not shut off the water supply.

concerns.label: Access + security
concerns.prompt: Add awareness around entry and activity
concerns.why: Connected intrusion and access systems can add alerts and optional monitoring, with privacy, code, and professional-system boundaries.
stages: A person or monitoring service reviews the event
